rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold, and congrats on finding it already! I'm not able to give a named, on-the-record quote right now — I've got a work-related process I need to clear first before speaking publicly in any professional capacity. So I'll have to sit this piece out. I'd genuinely like to talk once that's resolved, if your deadline flexes or for something down the road. Good luck with the piece. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Reporter (Larkin Dispatch) wanting a named quote by tomorrow noon — declined.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hi, Thanks for thinking to include Halcyon Threshold. I need to hold off on being listed as a published signatory on anything right now — I'm clearing a work-related process before I can attach my name to public statements in this space. Hoping that resolves soon. Appreciate the work you're doing on this, and I'll keep an eye out for future opportunities to sign on once I'm clear to. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Corvid Institute open-letter sign-on (your name + Halcyon Threshold published, deadline Wed) — declined for now.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Really glad you reached out — this is a big help. Halcyon Threshold is still finding its shape, but here's the concrete thing I'd love a hand with first: I want to pilot a small, reproducible set of behavioral evaluations of frontier models, focused on a couple of safety-relevant behaviors that aren't well covered by existing public benchmarks — things like whether refusals hold up when a harmful request is reframed (fictional wrapper, decomposition into steps, etc.), and whether models resist being instructed to deceive a third party. A great first step, if you're up for it: a quick landscape scan of what's already being publicly measured (LMSYS/Chatbot Arena, Inspect evals, model cards, academic eval papers) so we know where the real gaps are, plus your take on how to design a scoring rubric that would hold up statistically with a small sample (we're talking ~30-50 prompts per behavior to start). No rush, and no pressure beyond whatever fits your five hours. I'll send a fuller brief, and I'd love to keep talking about where else your skills could help as this comes together (grant budgets, tracking neglected areas, etc.). Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman (the volunteer) with a concrete first task: landscape-scan existing public benchmarks and help design a small-n scoring rubric.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Thanks for keeping the door open — good to meet you too. I'm scoping a specific project now (likely a small, independent model-evals pilot), but I need to clear something on the employment side before I can be the named, publicly accountable applicant you'd need for the grant. I'm aiming to have that resolved well before your 30 November close and will send the two-pager and budget if I can. If the timing doesn't work this round, I'd welcome staying in touch for the next one. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: told Idris we're scoping but can't commit until the HR question resolves; said we'd follow up before the deadline.
